text.p: Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) has approved several petrochemical expansion projects at its affiliates, the firm said in a release received on Sunday.
New projects include Arabian Petrochemical Company's (Petrokemya) olefins complex consisting of an 800,000 tonnes a year ethylene cracker and 275,000 tonnes a year propylene plant, the company said.

Eastern Petrochemical Company (Sharq) has been given approval for a 450,000 tonnes a year ethylene glycol plant and to increase linear low density polyethylene output by 300,000 tonnes a year through debottlenecking.
Sharq is a 50-50 SABIC joint venture with a consortium of Japanese companies led by Mitsubishi Corp.
Petrokemya and Saudi Petrochemical Company (Sadaf) -- a SABIC joint venture with Pecten Arabian Company, a subsidiary of U.S. Shell Oil Company, will set up a 500,000 tonnes a year styrene plant.
"The Kingdom stands to benefit immensely from these industrial investments aimed at manufacturing value-added products," said SABIC vice chairman and managing director Ibrahim Ibn Salamah.
